reader.notes: GR3a, b1 and b2 each picked the right object at run time and both ambiguity forms were refused. Nit: when B's own non-file name hides a global file-name, the OPEN refusal says no SELECT or file description entry in this source element gives the name, without naming the hider (the report verbs now name it); the program is still correctly refused. The same probes at --std 2023 (g1-sets, g1-local-qualifier-elem, g3-local-and-global-qualified, g3-two-globals-in-a, g1-cond-global-qualified-beside-own-data) print the same results.

refuter.evidence: Tier probes at --std 85 (the same output at --std 2023 where the program is legal there) under E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-fixed/out/refute-1985-f01/src/: g-local-beats-two-globals printed 'b 1 2' (one local plus two of A's globals: B's wins and is not an ambiguity, GR3a); g-local-cond-beats-two-globals printed B-COND (B's level-88 wins over A's two data items); g-b1-beats-two-outer printed 'a 2' (A's one global beats two of the outer program's, GR3b1); g-b1-index printed 'B: c / A: c / O: o' (index-names follow the data-name rules, X.1.3.8.3: B's IX is A's, the outer IX untouched); g-b2-chain printed O1 (A declares X without GLOBAL, the outer O and outermost OO each declare a global X: the nearest valid one wins); g-own-index-hides-global-data refused COBOL1637 (MOVE 7 TO IX in B names B's index-name, not A's global data IX); g-own-data-hides-global-index refused COBOL2112 (SET K UP BY 1 names B's data K, not A's global index K); g-own-data-global-cond-if refused COBOL2318 (IF X names B's data X, not A's global 88 X); g-outer-cond-own-data-unqual printed 'c' then A-COND. Reading stated for g-b2-chain: when A declares the name without GLOBAL, b1 has no object of A among the identified ones, and b2's 'until a single valid name has been found' carries the search outward, so O's X is right. Nit outside this rule: the COBOL2326 text for SET K TO 3 (K an integer data item) quotes VI.6.23.3 SR2 though K satisfies SR2; the refusal itself is right because the 1985 general rules forbid integer-1 when identifier-1 is not an index data item (cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.23.4 GR3c). cite.py: OK §1985:X.1.3.8.2 GR3 (until a single valid name has been found).
